I farm only 8 mu, but I run a wheat-maize rotation with well irrigation, and I have enough farming experience to manage it intensively. Because my education level is high and some family labor is tied up off-farm, I will keep the system simple, reliable, and yield-focused rather than labor-heavy. I will split the full 8 mu across the two seasonal crops in rotation, meaning the same land grows winter wheat first and then summer maize. I will use improved or hybrid seed because on a small irrigated farm I care more about stable output than saving seed. For wheat, I will apply moderate-to-high nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate at key growth stages, and use rotary tillage because it is efficient and fits a small farm. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, a bit more nitrogen than wheat, maintain balanced phosphorus and potassium, irrigate when summer rainfall is not enough, and keep pesticide use practical rather than excessive. My decisions are aimed at protecting yield, controlling labor needs, and making full use of irrigation on a small but intensively managed farm.
